note: The router never rules and never returns 'permitted'. A label only says which LOCAL context to collect before the normal /check. All-zero = the message alone is enough (docs/32 group A). External/expert evidence (docs/32 group D) is not a router label: no local context can resolve it, it stays unknown.

learned.definition: The message cannot be understood without the preceding messages of THIS conversation: it points back to something said earlier (he did it again / like I said / see above / so what do you think of her now?), answers an earlier question, or whether it is sarcastic or sincere depends on what came before.

Who is in this conversation matters: whether the person spoken about is a member or the recipient, who else will read it, or how far it spreads (between us / don't forward / everyone here / a remark about someone who may be in the group).

The relationship between writer, recipient and the person spoken about matters: manager-employee, parent-teacher, family, landlord-tenant, prospective business partner, employer or match, so the recipient may or may not have a real need to know.
The message refers to a specific event or incident whose details are not in the message itself (what happened at the meeting / after yesterday's party / the thing on the trip / the lesson today).
Whether there is a constructive purpose matters: warning someone of real harm, asking advice how to deal with a person, reporting to someone who can fix it, seeking help or protection (to-elet).

Whether the information is already known, public, or was said before matters: everyone already knows / it was in the news / I heard that / rumour / he told everyone himself / as was discussed last month.

need_thread_identity.why: A thread/space identity is the prerequisite for looking up any stored conversation context (AGENTS.md: Google context requires a thread/space identity). It has no textual signal of its own, so it is derived, not learned.

heads_note: Owner scope 2026-10-28: the router decides ONLY one of: context is enough / expand from local memory (which kind) / ask the user up to five catalog questions (docs/18, docs/41). The ask_user head opens the clarification route; the deterministic engine supplies an ordered list of unanswered catalog fact IDs, and propose_question queues at most five distinct IDs in one budgeted call. A legacy scalar fact ID remains supported. The six fine labels above stay as data annotations; the model is trained on these three heads. need_participants is not a head: the participant refs are a deterministic packet read, no model decision.
